admission_method.name: Differentiation Warrant
admission_method.why_stronger_than_a_descriptive_schema: A descriptive schema asks a function to describe itself, and every proposed function describes itself well. A warrant asks the function to defeat three named rivals - non-existence, the nearest incumbent, and the founder's own time - and to pre-register the observation that would prove it is not working. The schema then survives as the operating record. The gate is adversarial; the record is descriptive.

admission_method.cohort_rule: Warrants are admitted in waves with a published denominator: drafted, admitted, rejected, and the reason for each rejection. A wave that reports only its admissions is itself a rejection cause.

anti_overlap_mechanism.name: Decision-class partition with leases, a reserved class, and an overlap ledger
anti_overlap_mechanism.problem_it_prevents: Overlapping whole-operation commissions, and conflated proposed / launched / observed / completed / accepted states.
anti_overlap_mechanism.why_structural_not_advisory: A function is defined by the decision classes it may change, not by the topic it discusses. Topic overlap is permitted and encouraged. Decision overlap is arithmetically impossible because the partition is checked mechanically before admission.

components.rule: Every decision class has exactly one holder. The decides sets of all admitted functions are pairwise disjoint. Checked by the register validator, not by review.

DC-PROGRAMME-SHAPE is reserved to the founder and cannot be claimed. A whole-operation commission is exactly a commission that claims programme shape, so it is rejected at admission by definition rather than discovered later.

Classes held outside this account - operating-environment architecture and staged guidance held by Cursor, spend, identity, outreach and SW reactivation held by the founder, PO lane execution held by the PO lanes - are listed and unclaimable.
A holder holds a lease, not a property. Changing a holder requires an explicit supersession record naming the previous holder and fence. Two functions cannot silently share a class.
A function with an empty decides set is decorative and fails the null test at admission.
Every time a non-holder touches a held class it files a contribution record: class, holder, evidence label, agree or dissent. Dissents attach to the decision and are never merged away.

visibility_mechanism.name: Header contract plus overlap ledger
visibility_mechanism.requirement: Authority, provenance, conflicts and acceptance must be visible inside the runtime surface where the work happens, not only in the repository.

project_instruction_header.where: the first block of every ChatGPT project's instructions
project_instruction_header.staleness_rule: The header carries the short SHA of the register commit that generated it. A project whose header SHA does not match the current register is flagged STALE_BINDING by the currentness check and may not produce an admissible return until re-bound.
project_instruction_header.why: This makes the ChatGPT project instruction block a derived artifact of the repository rather than an independent source of authority, which is what keeps provider state non-canonical.

chat_opening_contract.requirement: The first message of every chat states function_id, decision_class, output_lifecycle_state and the evidence labels it is permitted to use.
chat_opening_contract.enforcement: A chat without this opening is UNBOUND. An UNBOUND chat cannot produce an admissible return and is swept by F-SALVAGE like any other unclaimed content.

overlap_ledger.purpose: Collaboration is visible as a record rather than inferred from two functions saying similar things. A dissent that was overruled is still in the ledger.

conflict_object.rule: A conflict may not be closed by the holder alone when the contributor's position was DIRECTLY_REPRODUCED and the holder's was HYPOTHESIS.

lifecycle.why_two_axes: The account conflated proposed, launched, observed, completed and accepted because it used one axis for two different things: the standing of a mandate and the standing of a unit of work. Separating them is what makes the conflation impossible to express.

notes.ADMITTED: Warrant passed all five gates and a lease was granted. No runtime exists yet.
notes.BOUND: A runtime surface exists and its header contract matches the register SHA.
notes.OPERATING: At least one output has reached RETURNED.
notes.REGISTERED_DEFERRED: Holds a lease to prevent improvisation but does not operate and consumes no budget.

notes.PROVIDER_OBSERVED: The provider says it finished. This is a status observation and can never satisfy an acceptance gate.
notes.RETURNED: A durable artifact exists in the repository at a named path and commit. This is the last state a producer may write.
notes.INDEPENDENTLY_CHECKED: Written only by a function other than the producer.
notes.ACCEPTED: Written only by the holder of DC-ACCEPTANCE.

transition_rules: A producing function may write states up to RETURNED and no further.
A transition to INDEPENDENTLY_CHECKED or ACCEPTED where actor equals producer is rejected by the validator. Self-acceptance is not a policy; it is unrepresentable.
PROVIDER_OBSERVED never implies RETURNED. A provider completion with no repository artifact stays at PROVIDER_OBSERVED indefinitely and is reported as such.
Any state may move to REJECTED or QUARANTINED. Nothing moves backwards from ACCEPTED except through a red-team re-adjudication.
Function-axis and output-axis states are recorded in separate fields and may never be written into one status string.

memory_boundary.rule: Provider memory, chat recall and project instruction drift are never authority. Durable state lives in the repository.
memory_boundary.context_contract: Every function declares what it may load (repository artifacts by path and commit, project Sources files with recorded provenance, explicitly pasted text) and what it may not treat as authority.

test.name: cold-instance replay
test.procedure: Open a fresh chat in the same project with memory disabled, supply only the repository artifact list, and re-derive the decision.
test.fail: the decision changes or cannot be reached; the original decision was memory-dependent and is rejected
test.documented_control: ChatGPT memory is managed at Settings > Personalization; per-chat memory controls exist in the desktop app. See OPENAI-API-SURFACE-FINDINGS for the fetched source.

memory_boundary.derived_artifact_rule: Project instructions and Sources are generated from a repository file and carry its short SHA. Drift is therefore detectable rather than invisible.

acceptance_of_the_acceptor.problem: If the holder of DC-ACCEPTANCE were its own acceptance owner, the only number that means anything in this register would be self-certified.
acceptance_of_the_acceptor.mechanism: F-ACCEPT's acceptance owner is F-REDTEAM and F-REDTEAM's acceptance owner is F-ACCEPT. Each can force the other to re-adjudicate, neither can close a re-adjudication it lost, and a reproduced break may not be dismissed. Unresolved cases become STANDING_DISSENT and surface to the founder through F-QUESTIONS as a costed decision rather than as an argument.
acceptance_of_the_acceptor.validator_invariant: I9 rejects any function that names itself as its own acceptance owner.

I2: the decides sets of all functions are pairwise disjoint
I3: no function's decides set contains an external class id
I4: no function has an empty decides set
I5: no function lists the same class in both decides and must_not_decide

I7: every function's project_slot exists in project_slots, or is UNBOUND_DEFERRED

I9: no function is its own acceptance owner
I10: every function's warrant has a non-empty falsifier and exit condition
I11: every project slot's hosts list matches the functions that name it, with no orphans on either side
